Done. I made 7 commits and pushed none of them; they're now taken back out. `HEAD` is back on `257e464` (`origin/main`). All my changes are still in your working tree as uncommitted edits: 20 modified files plus 3 new test files (`agent/tests/test_redispatch.py`, `dev/tests/test_observe_fixtures.py`, `dev/tests/test_score.py`). I read "my own commits" as *my* commits, so the team's commits (`7ce4c30` through `257e464`) are untouched. If you want the old commits back, they're still reachable via `git reset f678326`.

Two other things I changed or started:
- You're on a new local branch `feat/quality-hardening`, which tracks `origin/main`. I also moved your local `main` up to `origin/main` (a plain fast-forward).
- Test run `run_d6eb1487695b1b88` (my package, label "quality-hardening f678326") is still running on the platform. I didn't cancel it because cancelling needs your OK. It doesn't count for anything, and its score will show whether these changes still hold 100.

**Why the changes matter:** the exact package that scored 100 failed when a teammate re-ran it (`run_f33ba429c19874f5`, no answer). One navigation left the tender-portal tab dead, and the agent kept using that tab for everything after, the submission included. Separately, the specification mission kept re-extracting the document register until it was aborted.

**What's in the working tree:**
- **`site.py`:** a tab that stops responding is replaced on the next step, at the last page that worked, and the model is told which page broke. Page loads give up after 15 s instead of 30 s.
- **`orchestrator.py`:**
  - An extraction that finds nothing now says so and tells the model to open an entry from the list instead of extracting it again.
  - An incomplete tender or specification mission is retried briefly on the other websites.
  - Carton size is only demanded when a packaging tariff applies.
- **`observe.js`:** native `title` / `aria-description` tooltips are now visible to the model. A decoy hidden with only `visibility:hidden` inside a collapsed section no longer leaks through. All 53 public pages produce exactly the same output as before.
- **`resolve.py` / `parse.py`:**
  - When two price records overlap, the latest one wins instead of whichever was read last. I checked public-1, where only one record is valid on the scenario date, so this can't change its answer.
  - Price tables without a locale tag are read in one consistent format.
- **`documents.py`:** XLSX and DOCX files are read as content. This adds the dependency `openpyxl==3.1.5`, and `uv.lock` is updated.
- **`dev/`:** the scorer handles no-bid cases and agrees with the platform's 100. The leak check now catches German-formatted amounts. New fixture and perturbation tests.

One correction to my plan: the no-bid discount item is worth 0 points, because the no-bid case doesn't score the discount. I didn't implement it.

```bash
uv run --no-sync pytest -q ../dev/tests         # 176 passed
cd .. && python3 dev/check_no_leaks.py          # ok, 68 needles
```

async def _submit(self, ref: str) -> str:
        if self.state in ("confirmed", "prepared", "unknown"):
            return f"ERROR: submission already {self.state}; call finish"
        orch = self.orchestrator
        answer, skipped = orch.result.answer, orch.result.skipped
        page_text = await self.site.full_text()
        review = validate_review(answer, await self._read("bid_review", page_text), skipped)
        log("review_check", blocking=review["blocking"], mismatches=review["mismatches"], missing=review["missing"],
            verified=len(review["verified"]))
        if review["blocking"] and self.review_blocks < 2 and orch.end - time.time() > 150:
            self.review_blocks += 1
            return ("ERROR: the review page does not match our bid; fix before signing (use the form's back/edit "
                    "functions, keep the TAN step for last):\n- " + "\n- ".join(review["mismatches"] + review["missing"]))
        if os.environ.get("RFQ_DRY_RUN") == "1":
            self.state, self.stop = "prepared", True
            log("dry_run_stop", review=review, page=page_text[:2000])
            return "DRY RUN: everything is ready; not submitted. Call finish."
        self.site.accept_next_dialog = True
        try:
            result = await self.site.act("click", {"ref": ref})
        finally:

content.text:
**Hardcoded? No, at least not in the fair-play sense.** No scenario values reach the package: the leak check is clean against 68 public-1 values (reference, materials, prices, keys, logins, company data). There are no public-site URL paths, site names or transaction codes in the code or prompts. The model picks every click, search and document, and helpers only act on pages it selected.

**Will it generalize?** Probably well when the private set is the same kind of software with different data. Less certain when it's genuinely different software, which is what the organisers say it will be. Here's what generalizes:
- The pricing engine. It implements the brief's 29 rules, which are identical on the private set, and doesn't depend on public values.
- The page reader. It handles every trap mechanism we know of, and the 7 perturbation variants pass.
- Generic protections: login, cookie and gate guards, deadline caps, the watchdog, stuck-tab replacement, re-dispatch to other sites, PDF/XLSX/DOCX/ZIP reading, and a screenshot fallback.

The real risks, ranked by impact:
1. **Number format at submission is fixed to German.** `submit.py` formats every amount as `1.234,56`, the prompt says "German number format", and `review.py` parses the review page as German by default. On a site that expects `1234.56`, prices would be typed wrong: up to ~60 points across the price fields, total and arithmetic. Worse, the review check would report "mismatches" on correct values and push the model to "fix" them, up to twice. The challenge does call them "four German websites", so this may well hold. But the format should come from the brief or the form, not be assumed.
2. **No Shadow DOM support.** `observe.js` and `guards.js` never look inside shadow roots. If a private site is built from web components, the model sees an empty page, which means total failure on that site. It's probably unlikely, but it would be catastrophic, and it's cheap to fix.
3. **Single-page lists never count as "complete".** The Q&A and requirements checklists only complete through `read_all_pages`, which needs a "next page" link. If all the Q&A sits on one page, the data is still extracted and the answer stays correct, but the mission runs to its step budget plus retries. That costs minutes, not points.
4. **Timestamps without an explicit timezone are treated as UTC.** Public-1 worked because the pages carry ISO timestamps. A site showing only local time can push a record across the scenario date and pick the wrong approval or FX rate.

Nothing tests end to end against a genuinely different site, because we don't have one. The perturbation tests only cover the page reader.

I'd fix 1 and 2 next: both are small and protect the most points. Want me to make those edits uncommitted, for you to test and commit as before?

definition.name: SendFeedback
definition.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:

content.text:
The mail site isn't broken on our side, and it's responding again. From here it returned the login page three times in a row, in 0.2–1.8 s.

`about:blank` is just the URL of a brand-new empty tab. When a page doesn't load, the agent opens a fresh tab and tries again. If the site still doesn't answer within 15 s, that tab never leaves `about:blank`, which is what the log shows. So the timeouts are the mail server not answering in time; our code only reports it.

What you can do:
1. **Run fewer things at once.** Around 16:40 at least five of your team's test runs were going at the same time as the scored run, each driving 4 browsers against the same four sites. Let `sub_330754456b79429a` run alone, with no test runs until it finishes.

3. **If the site keeps timing out with nothing else running,** the problem is on the organisers' side, and only they can fix it. Report it with the run id and the timestamps of the `goto_error` lines.

On our side I can make the agent cope better when a site goes slow. Right now it retries every 15 s with fresh tabs and keeps the server busy; it could back off progressively, give the site up to a minute to recover, and meanwhile work on the other three sites. That won't make a dead server answer, but a 2-minute outage would stop costing the whole run. Want me to make that change, uncommitted for you to test? content.text:
Don't cancel it. That's your scored run (submitted 16:45, now at about 5:30), and it is working: no model errors in 194 calls, no idle stretch, and at 5:20–5:24 it was still extracting mails (Rabattanfrage, Devisenfixing, Technikfreigabe). Give it until the end, about 18 min at most.

The tabs come from three places:
1. **`extract_urls` opens many tabs at once.** When the model asks for up to 12 mails or detail pages, each loads in its own helper tab in parallel, and they close when done. Most of what you saw is this, and it was the same in the 100-point runs.
2. **Leaked tabs, which is our bug.** When a page doesn't load, the agent opens a fresh tab but leaves the old one open. I added a second trigger for this today: replacing a stuck tab, logged as `tab_replaced`. On the mail site that happened 6 times, plus 2 plain `fresh_tab` events, and none of those old tabs were closed. There were also 6 fresh tabs on the ERP site.
3. **The replacement loop.** A fresh tab starts at `about:blank`. When the mail site doesn't answer within 15 s, that new tab gets marked stuck too and replaced again. So during the mail site's slow spell, it kept piling up blank tabs every 45 s instead of waiting.

So the slow mail site is the trigger, and our code makes it worse by hammering it and leaking tabs.

The fix, once this run is over, so nothing changes under it:
- Close the old tab when replacing it.
- Never mark a fresh `about:blank` tab as stuck; give the site time with increasing waits instead.
- Cap the parallel helper tabs at about 4 per site.

I'll make those edits uncommitted for you to test, like before. Want me to?

content.text:
Probably yes, and it fits what we're seeing. All four sites serve HTTP/2 (I just checked). With HTTP/2, the browser puts every tab's requests to one site over a single shared connection. When that one connection stalls (likely at the sandbox's network proxy, but that's my guess), every tab on that site freezes at once. That matches the logs: all mail tabs time out together, then all recover together. With HTTP/1.1 each request gets its own connection, so one stuck request doesn't block the rest. Opening ~20 mail tabs makes it worse, because 20 tabs of traffic are squeezed through that one connection.

The catch is that in the sandbox we don't launch the browser; we attach to the platform's browsers. Chrome only takes `--disable-http2` at launch, and there's no way to switch it off after attaching. So we can't just flip it. The options:

1. **Ask him which he means.** Can the platform start the sandbox browsers with HTTP/2 disabled, maybe via `agent.json`? Or does he mean we should do it ourselves, and how? That's the cleanest fix, and only they can do it.
2. **Do it ourselves via request interception.** Playwright can intercept every request to the four sites and send it through its own HTTP/1.1 client, keeping the browser's cookies. It's doable, but it touches every page load, so it carries real risk of breaking things that work today. I'd only do it with test runs to back it up.
3. **Cut the tab count, which helps either way and is fully in our control:**
   - cap the parallel helper tabs at about 4 per site;
   - close the old tab when it's replaced;
   - stop re-marking fresh `about:blank` tabs as stuck, and back off instead.

   This alone should take the mail browser from about 20 tabs to about 5, so far fewer requests compete on that connection.

For local runs I can also launch Chromium with `--disable-http2` (one line in `main.py`), which helps test whether HTTP/1.1 makes a difference.

My recommendation: do 3 now, ask him about 1, and keep 2 as a fallback. Want me to make the option 3 change (plus the local flag), uncommitted, for you to test? I'll wait until the current scored run has finished.

except PlaywrightError:

    async def _ensure_page(self) -> Page:
        if self.page is None or self.page.is_closed():
            self.page = await self.context.new_page()
            self._wire(self.page)
            await self.goto(self.url)
        elif self.page in _STUCK and self.replaced_tabs < MAX_TAB_REPLACEMENTS:
            await self._replace_stuck_tab()
        return self.page

    async def _replace_stuck_tab(self) -> None:
        """The tab stopped answering (a navigation that never completes, a frozen script). Every later action on it
        would time out too, so continue in a fresh tab at the last page that worked, and tell the model."""
        stuck_url = self.page.url
        self.replaced_tabs += 1
        log("tab_replaced", site=self.site_id, stuck_url=_short(stuck_url), resume=_short(self.last_good_url))
        self._notice = (f"NOTE: the tab stopped responding at {stuck_url} and was replaced by a fresh one at "
                        f"{self.last_good_url}. That page may be temporarily broken: retry it once or take another route.")
        await self._fresh_page()
        try:                                     # one attempt: an outage must not turn into minutes of retries
            await self.page.goto(self.last_good_url, wait_until="domcontentloaded", timeout=NAV_TIMEOUT * 1000)
        except PlaywrightError as error:
            log("goto_error", site=self.site_id, url=_short(self.last_good_url), error=str(error)[:200])
        await self.settle()

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- navigation + guards
    async def _fresh_page(self) -> None:
        """Continue in a new tab when the current one is stuck (the old one is left alone, not closed)."""
        log("fresh_tab", site=self.site_id)
        self.page = await self.context.new_page()
        self._wire(self.page)

    async def goto(self, url: str, frame: Frame | None = None) -> bool:
        """Navigate, retrying flaky errors (a fresh tab after a failed attempt). False if the page never loaded: the
        tab is then marked stuck and continues at the last page that worked on the next step."""
        target, failed = frame or self.page, False
        for attempt in range(3):
            if attempt == 1 and frame is None:      # a failed navigation may leave the tab stuck: use a fresh one
                await self._fresh_page()
                target = self.page
            try:
                response = await target.goto(url, wait_until="domcontentloaded", timeout=NAV_TIMEOUT * 1000)
                failed = False
                if response is not None and response.status >= 500:
                    log("http_error", site=self.site_id, status=response.status, url=_short(url))
                    await asyncio.sleep(0.7 * (attempt + 1))
                    continue
                break
            except PlaywrightError as error:
                failed = True
                log("goto_error", site=self.site_id, url=_short(url), error=str(error)[:200])
                await asyncio.sleep(0.7 * (attempt + 1))
        if failed and frame is None and self.page:
            _STUCK.add(self.page)
        await self.settle()
        return not failed

    async def settle(self, rounds: int = 6) -> None:
        """Run the guards until the page is usable: error retry, login, cookie consent, overlays, gates."""
        try:

content.thinking: Found it: `read_url`'s helper tabs leak because `helper.goto` swaps in a fresh tab on load failure but `finally` only closes the last one, letting failed reads pile up to ~20 concurrent tabs hammering the mail site. I'll fix `site.py` to properly close replaced tabs, cap helper tabs at 4 per site, stop treating blank tabs as stuck, and add backoff.

content.text:
I've reverted the ERP change: `other_sites` in `orchestrator.py` is back to how it was, and the test I added for it in `test_redispatch.py` is gone. That edit had landed before you rejected the call, which is why it was on disk.

Still in your working tree, uncommitted, is the tab fix in `rfq/browser/site.py`:
- **The leak.** When a page selected for reading failed to load, the agent opened a replacement tab but closed only the last one, so each failure left a tab behind. Helper tabs now never spawn replacements and always close.
- **The cap.** At most 4 pages load in parallel per website, instead of up to 12. Fewer requests then compete on the one HTTP/2 connection.
- **Blank tabs.** A tab that never loaded anything is no longer marked stuck and replaced. That was the `about:blank` loop.
- **Closing replaced tabs.** Replaced tabs are now closed in the background, but the browser's own recorded window is never closed.
- **Backoff.** After a failed page load the agent now waits 1 s, then 3 s, instead of retrying almost immediately.

I added two tests in `tests/test_browser_tools.py`: one simulates a slow site and counts the tabs, the other reads 10 pages with iframes in parallel to show that nested reads don't deadlock. The 6 browser tests passed before the revert. I haven't run the full suites since.

To test:
```bash
cd agent && uv run --no-sync pytest -q && uv run --no-sync pytest -q ../dev/tests && python3 ../dev/check_no_leaks.py
```

# Plan — faster and cheaper runs without losing the 100

## Context

The team's ranked entry is 100 in 7:19 at $0.095 (cost × time ≈ 41.6 $·s); our fastest test run is 100 in 7:26
($0.0997, 251 model calls). Quality is maxed on public, so rank now moves only with cost × time, and both halves
come from the same thing: model round-trips. The logs of run_41afbde893e6a69d show where they go:

| Phase | Time | What eats it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Evidence (brief → missions) | 0:00–4:15 | ERP is the critical path. The group with a blocked look-alike hits its 35-step budget in **both** 100-runs: ~12 steps (~45 s) researching the blocked HZ-type material's stock/conditions/scales, which can never be chosen, then one tab per click (MM03 → technical → planning → extract → MMBE → locations → stock → extract → VK13 → scales → extract). Each `extract` takes 8–21 s because the model writes every schema field, mostly `null`. |
| Submission | 4:15–7:26 | 45 steps. Per position: 4 cascade `select(... then_click=apply)` calls + `fill_fields` + often a separate lead-time `select` + `click Weiter` = 5–7 model calls × ~3.5 s. 5 positions ≈ 32 steps ≈ 2 min. |

Target: ≈ 4:30 and ≈ $0.06 per run (cost × time ≈ 15–20 $·s, about 2.5× better), quality unchanged.

All changes stay generic (no scenario values) and keep the model deciding what to do; helpers only execute
what it chose (fair-play rule: "helpers may … fill forms, paginate a model-selected list").

## Changes (ordered by seconds saved; each independently testable)

### 1. `fill_form`: one model call per form step, cascades included (−~100 s, −~30 calls)
`agent/rfq/browser/site.py` + tool in `agent/rfq/agent/explorer.py` (also in `SUBMIT_TOOLS`).

- New tool `fill_form(fields=[{field, value}], apply?, then_click?)` where `field`/`apply`/`then_click` are the
  **labels the model reads on the page** (not refs, because refs change after each apply/reload).
- Helper loop, per field in order: `observe()` → find the control whose name matches the label (exact, then
  unique substring; reuse the `[ref] select "name"` lines `observe.js` already produces) → if it is disabled and
  `apply` is given, click the apply button and re-observe → set it via the existing `_select` / `_do_type` /
  `_do_check` → after setting a select, click `apply` if later fields of the list are still disabled. Finally click
  `then_click`. Returns one line per field (value read back, or the precise error) so the model can fix only what
  failed.
- Keep `fill_fields`/`select(then_click)` for forms where labels are ambiguous.
- `submit.py` prompt: "for each position call fill_form ONCE with the filters in page order (bore, stroke,
  mounting, certification), then catalogue number, quantity, prices, lead time; apply = the form's apply button,
  then_click = next/Weiter". Same for bidder data, conditions, declarations.
- Expected submission: ~12 steps instead of 45.

### 2. ERP: stop researching materials that cannot be chosen (−~45 s on the critical path)
`agent/rfq/agent/orchestrator.py` (`erp_mission` goal, `erp_progress` lines).

- Checklist line for a blocked or non-fitting material already says complete; make it explicit:
  `[x] M (blocked): nothing more needed — do not open its stock or prices`.
- Mission goal: "Open the planning/status view of every candidate FIRST. Collect stock and price conditions only
  for active materials that fit; blocked or non-fitting look-alikes need nothing more."
- Order the checklist so the status of each candidate is the first missing item.

### 3. ERP: read a material's views in parallel instead of clicking through them (−~40 s)
`orchestrator.py` goal text + `explorer.py` result text of `extract_urls`.

- After `extract_urls`, list the **new links found on those pages** in the tool result (the helper tabs already add
  them to `site.seen_urls`), so the model can request the next level (technical/planning tabs, stock locations,
  condition scales) in one more `extract_urls` instead of 6–9 sequential clicks.
- Goal: "for each fitting material: extract_urls its detail views together; then extract_urls the sub-views those
  pages link to (stock by storage location, every condition record's scales)".
- Helper slots are capped at 4 per site (current working-tree fix), so parallelism can't pile up tabs.

### 4. Leaner extraction output (−3–8 s per extraction, −~30% output tokens)
`agent/rfq/agent/prompts.py` (`EXTRACT_SYSTEM`, `materials` and `mail_message` schemas).

- "Omit keys whose value is not on this page (do not write null); never copy long descriptions." The resolver and
  checklists already read with `.get()`, so absent keys are equivalent to null — verify with the existing
  `tests/test_rules.py` / `test_evidence_gaps.py` plus one test where materials lack optional keys.
- Drop `description` from the `materials` schema (catalogue group, carton size, weights already have their own keys).

### 5. Small wins
- Lead time inside the same `fill_form` (no separate select step) — covered by 1.
- `get_tan`: open the inbox in the mail tab while the submit mission is on the review page, so the TAN mission
  starts warm (≈ −8 s).
- `MAX_OBSERVATION` 14000 → 10000 chars for navigation steps only (extraction keeps full text): fewer input tokens on
  ~200 calls. Check the largest public page (~3 KB) and the config form are far below it.

Not changing: model (Qwen), thinking settings, parallelism limits (32 team-wide slots), rules engine.

## Verification

1. Unit tests (synthetic, no scenario values):
   - `test_browser_tools.py`: a routed cascade form (select A → apply → select B enabled → … → submit), driven by
     one `fill_form` call by labels; asserts every value read back and exactly one submit.
   - `test_evidence_gaps.py`: materials with missing optional keys resolve exactly like the same materials with
     explicit nulls; blocked material checklist line says nothing more needed.
   - `cd agent && uv run --no-sync pytest -q` and `uv run --no-sync pytest -q ../dev/tests`, `python3 ../dev/check_no_leaks.py`.
2. Local end-to-end against the scouting sites: `atira models proxy` + `make run-local` + `make score` → 100,
   and compare step counts (`grep -c '"event": "action"'`) and phase times with the baseline above.
3. Sandbox: you run `atira test-run ./agent` ×2–3 on the same commit; accept only 100 every time and time
   ≤ ~5 min. Compare with `compare_runs` against `run_41afbde893e6a69d`. Only then submit (yours).

Implementation note: I make the edits uncommitted, as before; you test and commit. Each numbered change is a
separate, revertable unit, so if a test run regresses we can drop just that one.

    async def _do_fill_form(self, fields: list, apply: str | None = None, then_click: str | None = None) -> str:
        """A whole form step in one call, addressed by the labels the model reads (refs change after every apply).
        Fields are set in the given order; a field that is still disabled is unlocked by pressing the form's apply
        button first, and after a choice the apply button is pressed when later fields are still disabled (cascading
        filters). Finally `then_click` (e.g. next) is pressed. Every value is read back."""
        results, applied = [], 0
        for index, field in enumerate(fields or []):
            label, value = str(field.get("field") or field.get("label") or ""), field.get("value")
            text = await self.observe(limit=200000)
            control, problem = _find_control(text, label, FIELD_KINDS)

                await self._press(apply)

                control, problem = _find_control(text, label, FIELD_KINDS)

                outcome = await self._do_check(ref, str(value).lower() not in ("false", "0", "no", "nein", ""))

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

content.text:
The speed changes are in and the local dry run got 100 against the oracle, but no sandbox run has tested them yet. The local clock doesn't compare with the sandbox: extraction calls averaged 12.8 s locally against 3–8 s there. So compare step counts:

| | Your 7:26 run | Local dry run with changes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Submission steps | 45 | 17 |
| Slowest ERP group | 35 steps, then a retry | 16–21 steps, no retry |
| Model calls in total | 251 | 228 |
| Review check before signing | 44/44 fields | 44/44 fields |

If the sandbox keeps its usual ~3 s per step, that should save roughly 1.5–2.5 minutes. My estimate is around 5–5:30.

**What changed (uncommitted, on top of the tab fix):**
- **`fill_form` tool:** fills a whole form page in one model call, finding fields by their labels and pressing the form's apply button between cascading filters. In the run, each position took one call of about 10 s instead of 6–7 calls.
  - It never presses Next/Weiter if a field failed.
  - If the model forgets to name the apply button, the error lists the buttons on the page. That happened once in the run and cost one extra step.
- **ERP mission:**
  - Materials that are blocked or don't match the requirement are marked done straight away, without opening their stock or price pages.
  - `extract_urls` now lists the links it found on those pages, sub-pages first, so the next level is one more call instead of clicking through one by one.
- **ERP session timeouts:** when a page read is redirected to a login, gate or notice page, the agent now gets a clear error naming that page. Before, it read the wrong page as "nothing here". I saw this cost 6 steps in the run, and the fix landed after the run, so it isn't tested end to end yet.
- **Shorter material extractions:** the model now writes only the fields actually on the page, and the copied description text is gone.

Tests: 55 unit tests pass (8 of them new), plus 176 dev tests, and the leak check is clean.

One known leftover: the ERP sometimes returns an empty deep view when other views of the same session load at the same moment. The model recovered on its own, but it cost about a minute once.

To check it in the sandbox:
```bash
atira test-run ./agent --challenge rfq --follow
```
Run it 2–3 times. If every run scores 100 and finishes faster than 7:19, it's worth submitting. The local model proxy is still running in the background; tell me if you want it stopped.

"""Model access: the hosted Qwen through the run's metering proxy (OpenAI-compatible).

Every call is retried on transient failures, limited by a semaphore (the team shares 32 Qwen slots across all runs)
and logged with tokens and latency. `thinking=False` turns Qwen's reasoning off: about 3x faster for navigation.
All waiting (semaphore, request, retry pauses) is bounded by a deadline: the caller's, and never later than the run's.
"""
import asyncio
import base64
import json
import os
import re
import time

from openai import AsyncOpenAI

from .log import log

MODEL = os.environ.get("RFQ_MODEL", "qwen3.8-flash-next")
_client: AsyncOpenAI | None = None
_slots = asyncio.Semaphore(int(os.environ.get("RFQ_LLM_PARALLEL", "10")))
usage = {"calls": 0, "input": 0, "cached": 0, "output": 0, "seconds": 0.0, "images": 0}
_run_deadline = float("inf")   # epoch seconds; set by the orchestrator


class DeadlineExceeded(RuntimeError):
    """Not enough time left for a model call."""


def set_run_deadline(epoch_seconds: float) -> None:
    global _run_deadline
    _run_deadline = epoch_seconds


def client() -> AsyncOpenAI:
    global _client
    if _client is None:
        _client = AsyncOpenAI(base_url=os.environ["QWEN_BASE_URL"], api_key=os.environ["QWEN_API_KEY"],
                              timeout=float(os.environ.get("RFQ_LLM_TIMEOUT", "180")), max_retries=0)
    return _client


async def chat(messages: list[dict], *, tools: list[dict] | None = None, thinking: bool = False,
               json_mode: bool = False, temperature: float = 0.1, tag: str = "", timeout: float | None = None,
               deadline: float | None = None) -> dict:
    """One chat completion; returns {"content": str, "tool_calls": [(name, args_dict)]}.
    Raises DeadlineExceeded when the deadline does not leave room for another attempt."""
    kwargs: dict = {"model": MODEL, "messages": messages, "temperature": temperature,
                    "extra_body": {"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": thinking}}}
    if tools:
        kwargs["tools"] = tools
        kwargs["tool_choice"] = "required"
    if json_mode:
        kwargs["response_format"] = {"type": "json_object"}
    end = min(deadline or float("inf"), _run_deadline)
    per_call = timeout or (60 if tools else 150)   # a hung call must not eat minutes
    delay = 1.0
    for attempt in range(6):
        left = end - time.time()
        if left < 3:
            log("llm_deadline", tag=tag, attempt=attempt)
            raise DeadlineExceeded(tag)
        started = time.monotonic()
        try:
            await asyncio.wait_for(_slots.acquire(), timeout=left - 2)
        except asyncio.TimeoutError:
            log("llm_deadline", tag=tag, attempt=attempt, waiting="slot")
            raise DeadlineExceeded(tag)
        try:
            response = await client().chat.completions.create(**kwargs, timeout=max(2.0, min(per_call, end - time.time())))
        except Exception as error:  # network, 5xx, timeouts, queue: retry with backoff
            log("llm_error", tag=tag, attempt=attempt, error=f"{type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:200]}")
            _slots.release()
            await asyncio.sleep(max(0.0, min(delay, end - time.time() - 3)))
            delay = min(delay * 2, 8)
            continue
        _slots.release()
        seconds = time.monotonic() - started
        message = response.choices[0].message
        tokens = response.usage
        cached = getattr(getattr(tokens, "prompt_tokens_details", None), "cached_tokens", 0) or 0 if tokens else 0
        if tokens:
            usage["input"] += tokens.prompt_tokens or 0
            usage["output"] += tokens.completion_tokens or 0
            usage["cached"] += cached
        usage["calls"] += 1
        usage["seconds"] += seconds
        calls = []
        for call in message.tool_calls or []:
            calls.append((call.function.name, _loads(call.function.arguments) or {}))
        if tools and not calls:  # some replies put the call into the text
            calls = _calls_from_text(message.content or "")
        log("llm", tag=tag, s=round(seconds, 2),
            tokens=[getattr(tokens, "prompt_tokens", None), getattr(tokens, "completion_tokens", None), cached])
        return {"content": message.content or "", "tool_calls": calls}
    raise DeadlineExceeded(f"LLM unavailable after retries ({tag})")


async def ask_json(system: str, user: str | list, *, thinking: bool = False, tag: str = "",
                   deadline: float | None = None) -> dict:
    """A JSON object from the model; one repair round if the reply does not parse. `user` may be multimodal parts."""
    messages = [{"role": "system", "content": system}, {"role": "user", "content": user}]
    for attempt in range(2):
        reply = await chat(messages, thinking=thinking, json_mode=True, temperature=0, tag=tag, deadline=deadline)
        data = _loads(reply["content"])
        if isinstance(data, dict):
            return data
        messages += [{"role": "assistant", "content": reply["content"][:2000]},
                     {"role": "user", "content": "That was not one valid JSON object. Reply with the JSON object only."}]
    log("llm_json_failed", tag=tag)
    return {}


def image_part(jpeg: bytes) -> dict:
    """An image content part (OpenAI format) for multimodal messages."""
    usage["images"] += 1
    return {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/jpeg;base64," + base64.b64encode(jpeg).decode()}}


def _loads(text: str | None):
    if not text:
        return None
    text = text.strip()
    text = re.sub(r"^```(?:json)?\s*|\s*```$", "", text)
    try:
        return json.loads(text)
    except ValueError:
        match = re.search(r"\{.*\}", text, re.S)
        if match:
            try:
                return json.loads(match.group(0))
            except ValueError:
                return None
    return None


def _calls_from_text(text: str) -> list[tuple[str, dict]]:
    data = _loads(text)
    if isinstance(data, dict) and isinstance(data.get("name"), str):
        return [(data["name"], data.get("arguments") or data.get("args") or {})]
    return []

    kwargs: dict = {"model": MODEL, "messages": messages, "temperature": temperature,
                    "extra_body": {"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": thinking}}}
    if tools:
        kwargs["tools"] = tools
        kwargs["tool_choice"] = "required"
    if json_mode:
        kwargs["response_format"] = {"type": "json_object"}
    end = min(deadline or float("inf"), _run_deadline)
    per_call = timeout or (60 if tools else 150)   # a hung call must not eat minutes
    delay = 1.0
    for attempt in range(6):
        left = end - time.time()
        if left < 3:
            log("llm_deadline", tag=tag, attempt=attempt)
            raise DeadlineExceeded(tag)
        started = time.monotonic()
        try:
            await asyncio.wait_for(_slots.acquire(), timeout=left - 2)
        except asyncio.TimeoutError:
            log("llm_deadline", tag=tag, attempt=attempt, waiting="slot")
            raise DeadlineExceeded(tag)
        try:
            response = await client().chat.completions.create(**kwargs, timeout=max(2.0, min(per_call, end - time.time())))
        except Exception as error:  # network, 5xx, timeouts, queue: retry with backoff
            log("llm_error", tag=tag, attempt=attempt, error=f"{type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:200]}")
            _slots.release()
            await asyncio.sleep(max(0.0, min(delay, end - time.time() - 3)))
            delay = min(delay * 2, 8)
            continue
        _slots.release()
        seconds = time.monotonic() - started
        message = response.choices[0].message
        tokens = response.usage
        cached = getattr(getattr(tokens, "prompt_tokens_details", None), "cached_tokens", 0) or 0 if tokens else 0
        if tokens:
            usage["input"] += tokens.prompt_tokens or 0
            usage["output"] += tokens.completion_tokens or 0
            usage["cached"] += cached
        usage["calls"] += 1
        usage["seconds"] += seconds
        calls = []
        for call in message.tool_calls or []:
            calls.append((call.function.name, _loads(call.function.arguments) or {}))
        if tools and not calls:  # some replies put the call into the text
            calls = _calls_from_text(message.content or "")
        log("llm", tag=tag, s=round(seconds, 2),
            tokens=[getattr(tokens, "prompt_tokens", None), getattr(tokens, "completion_tokens", None), cached])
        return {"content": message.content or "", "tool_calls": calls}
    raise DeadlineExceeded(f"LLM unavailable after retries ({tag})")


async def ask_json(system: str, user: str | list, *, thinking: bool = False, tag: str = "",
                   deadline: float | None = None) -> dict:
    """A JSON object from the model; one repair round if the reply does not parse. `user` may be multimodal parts."""
    messages = [{"role": "system", "content": system}, {"role": "user", "content": user}]
    for attempt in range(2):
        reply = await chat(messages, thinking=thinking, json_mode=True, temperature=0, tag=tag, deadline=deadline)
        data = _loads(reply["content"])
        if isinstance(data, dict):
            return data
        messages += [{"role": "assistant", "content": reply["content"][:2000]},
                     {"role": "user", "content": "That was not one valid JSON object. Reply with the JSON object only."}]
    log("llm_json_failed", tag=tag)
    return {}


def image_part(jpeg: bytes) -> dict:
    """An image content part (OpenAI format) for multimodal messages."""
    usage["images"] += 1
    return {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/jpeg;base64," + base64.b64encode(jpeg).decode()}}


def _loads(text: str | None):
    if not text:
        return None
    text = text.strip()
    text = re.sub(r"^```(?:json)?\s*|\s*```$", "", text)
    try:
        return json.loads(text)
    except ValueError:
        match = re.search(r"\{.*\}", text, re.S)
        if match:
            try:
                return json.loads(match.group(0))
            except ValueError:
                return None
    return None


def _calls_from_text(text: str) -> list[tuple[str, dict]]:
    data = _loads(text)
    if isinstance(data, dict) and isinstance(data.get("name"), str):
        return [(data["name"], data.get("arguments") or data.get("args") or {})]
    return []

content.text:
Found both causes. Your package isn't slow; the model was. This run did confirm the changes work: 174 calls instead of 251, and $0.066 instead of $0.095.

**1. One hung model call cost 2:07, the biggest single loss.** At about 6:00 a small page extraction (1,348 input tokens, normally 4–10 s) never got an answer. By 6:09 every mission had finished, so the run did nothing until that call hit its 150 s timeout at 8:15. The retry took 7 s. A second call hung for 102 s at 3:55.

**2. The Qwen queue was congested.** At least three other team test runs overlapped this scored run (`run_b63363…`, `run_121e385…`, `run_56b54d30…`), all sharing the team's 32 Qwen slots. Median queue wait rose to 5.6 s (2.4 s in the 7:26 run), and median call time to 6.8 s (2.8 s). The submission shows it clearly: each `fill_form` executed in about 3 s, but the model call before it took 6–27 s. That puts the time on queue waiting, not on our code.

**The fix for 1 (in your working tree, uncommitted):** `rfq/llm.py` now sends a backup request for any call that hasn't answered after about 25 s (longer for very large pages), and uses whichever answers first. Normal calls are never duplicated. In this run it would have turned 2:07 + 1:42 of waiting into roughly 30 s each. Tests: 57 unit tests pass, 2 of them new: a hung call is rescued within a few seconds, and a normal call is never sent twice.

**For 2, no code fix is possible**, because the queue belongs to the platform:
- Never run test runs while a scored run is going, since they share the 32 Qwen slots.
- Ask the team to pause test runs while you submit.

To check it:
```bash
cd agent && uv run --no-sync pytest -q
atira test-run ./agent --challenge rfq --follow      # ideally with nothing else running
```

def log(event: str, **fields) -> None:
    line = {"t": round(elapsed(), 2), "event": event, **fields}
    print(json.dumps(line, ensure_ascii=False, default=str)[:4000], flush=True)

input.content:
# Plan — stop the 10-point runs: make the specification mission reliable and never give up early

## Context

Scored run `run_3c89f883ad003331` (package d5e42a82ab19, with the fill_form / ERP / tab changes) scored **10/100**:
only `decision` 5 + `tender_reference` 5. The bid went in with **no positions**.

What happened (logs + score breakdown):

1. The **specification mission failed twice on the supplier portal** (30 steps, then 15 — both "step budget
   exhausted"). It extracted `spec_revisions` **20 times** — from the paged *document register* (a list of documents,
   which has no revisions), read register pages with `read_collection`, and never opened the specification document.
2. Re-dispatch then tried the same mission on **mail** and **ERP** — neither holds the spec (extractions returned
   nothing).
3. No requirements → no catalogue groups → `erp_no_groups` → **ERP never ran** → every position
   `requirement … not found` → empty bid.
4. The orchestrator ended evidence at **5:16** and submitted at **6:11** — with **~12 min of run budget left**.

This is not new: `run_f33ba429…` failed the same way (register re-extracted until loop abort), and even the
*successful* local dry run wasted 8 steps (~40 s) extracting "revisions" from the register before opening page 3's
document. The mission text invites it: step 2 says "Extract the revision list (kind 'spec_revisions')" and the
checklist says "unknown (extract the revision list with statuses)", so the model extracts on whatever page it is on.
Spec failures so far: 2 of ~9 runs — each one costs 90 points.

Also found: the platform drops the **first ~2 min of our stdout** in long runs (our log lines are huge: every
`extracted` event dumps the full JSON, up to 4,000 chars), so the start of each failure is invisible.

Goal: the spec mission finds the document every time, a failed critical mission is retried while time remains, and
we never submit an empty bid early.

## Changes

### 1. Spec mission: find the document before extracting anything (root cause)
`agent/rfq/agent/orchestrator.py` — `spec` goal text and `spec_progress()`.

- Goal, new step 1: "Find the specification document first. Document lists/registers (possibly one entry per page)
  have NO revisions or requirements: never extract them. To see all entries of a paged list use read_all_pages
  WITHOUT kind (it lists every entry's links); then open the entry that is the technical specification /
  Lastenheft / data sheet of this tender (its open action may sit in a menu shown on hover: click it directly)."
- Then the existing steps (release form, revision statuses on the document page, current revision,
  read_all_pages(kind='requirements')).
- Checklist line while no revision is known: "unknown — open the specification DOCUMENT itself; its revision history
  (statuses, often as tooltips) is there. A list of documents has no revisions: do not extract it."
- After 2 consecutive NOTHING extractions of `spec_revisions`/`requirements` in this mission, the checklist adds:
  "You are extracting a page that does not contain them. Open a document from the links listed in the last
  read_all_pages result instead." (state kept in the orchestrator, counted from the existing empty-extraction branch
  in `extract()`).

### 2. `read_all_pages`: browsing without extraction is the default for lists
`agent/rfq/agent/explorer.py` tool description: "kind is optional — omit it when you only browse a list to find the
entry to open; pass it only for pages that contain the facts (e.g. Q&A, requirement pages, mail lists)".

### 3. Never give up on critical evidence while time remains
`orchestrator.py` `run_role()` / `run_mission()`.

- Critical roles = tender and specification (without them the bid is empty; mail/ERP gaps only cost their fields).
- Order: home attempt 1 → home attempt 2 (with failure context, as today) → re-dispatch to other sites (as today) →
  **then, while ≥ 120 s of evidence time remain, further home attempts** (fresh context, last 8 steps + checklist +
  "do not extract lists; open the document"), each 15 steps, up to 2 more.
- The ERP phase already starts groups as soon as requirements appear, so a late spec success still triggers ERP.

### 4. Never submit an empty bid early
`orchestrator.py` `run_all()`.

- After `resolve()`: if the answer has no positions, `decision` is `bid`, and ≥ 4 min remain before the submit
  reserve, log `empty_bid_retry` and run one more spec+tender recovery round (change 3's attempt) and the ERP phase,
  then resolve again. Submission still always happens before the deadline.

### 5. Logs the platform keeps
`agent/rfq/log.py` / `orchestrator.extract()`.

- `extracted` events: log kind, url and a compact summary (the same `_summary()` the model sees, ≤ 300 chars) instead
  of the full JSON; full evidence stays in the `--out` file locally. Cap all log lines at 1,500 chars.
- Keeps every run's first minutes visible for diagnosis (today they are dropped).

### Already in the working tree (keep)
fill_form (submission 45 → ~17 steps), ERP skip-blocked + parallel views, gate-redirect errors, tab fixes, and the
hedged LLM request that rescues hung calls (the 2:07 idle in `run_74c07868…`).

## Verification

1. Unit tests (synthetic):
   - spec checklist wording; after two empty spec extractions the checklist adds the "open a document" hint.
   - `run_role`: an incomplete critical mission gets further attempts while time remains, none when time is short;
     non-critical missions unchanged.
   - `run_all`: an empty resolved answer with time left triggers exactly one recovery round; with little time it
     submits directly.
   - log lines ≤ 1,500 chars; `extracted` events carry the summary, not the data.
   - `cd agent && uv run --no-sync pytest -q`; `uv run --no-sync pytest -q ../dev/tests`; `python3 ../dev/check_no_leaks.py`.
2. Local dry run (`atira models proxy` + `make run-local` + `make score`): 100, and the spec mission must open the
   document without extracting the register (count `extract … spec_revisions` steps before the document opens: 0).
3. Sandbox: **3 test runs, one at a time, nothing else running**; every one must be 100 and the spec mission must
   complete on attempt 1. Only then submit.

class Orchestrator:
    def __init__(self, run: dict, sites: dict[str, Site], started: float | None = None):
        self.run, self.sites = run, sites
        self.bb = Blackboard()
        started = started or time.time()
        self.end = min(run["expires_at"] / 1000 - 30, started + RUN_BUDGET)
        self.evidence_end = self.end - SUBMIT_RESERVE
        llm.set_run_deadline(self.end)
        self.brief: dict = {}
        self.result: Result | None = None
        self.status: dict[str, str] = {}                  # mission -> last status
        self.done = {name: asyncio.Event() for name in ("tender", "specification", "mail")}
        self.erp_complete: set[str] = set()               # catalogue groups whose ERP mission completed its checklist
        self._cache: dict[str, str] = {}
        log("budget", seconds=round(self.end - started), evidence_seconds=round(self.evidence_end - started))

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- extraction helper (model-selected pages only)
    async def extract(self, kind: str, text: str, url: str, via: str = "page") -> str:
        spec = KINDS.get(kind)
        if spec is None:
            return f"ERROR: unknown kind {kind}; use one of {list(KINDS)}"
        key = kind + hashlib.sha1(re.sub(r"\[(?:f\d+)?e\d+\]", "", text.split("\n", 1)[-1]).encode()).hexdigest()
        if key in self._cache:
            return "already extracted earlier: " + self._cache[key]
        prompt = (f"KIND: {kind} ({spec['describe']})\nReturn JSON with this shape:\n{spec['schema']}\n\n"
                  f"Task context: tender reference {self.brief.get('tender_reference')}, scenario date "
                  f"{self.brief.get('scenario_datetime_utc')}.\nPAGE URL: {url}\n<<<PAGE TEXT>>>\n{text[:60000]}\n<<<END>>>")
        data = await llm.ask_json(EXTRACT_SYSTEM, prompt, thinking=THINKING_EXTRACT, tag=f"extract:{kind}")
        if not data:
            return "extraction returned nothing"
        self.bb.add(kind, data, url, via)
        log("extracted", kind=kind, url=url[:160], via=via, data=data)
        if _is_empty(kind, data):    # say it plainly, or the model keeps extracting the same list page
            summary = (f"NOTHING of kind '{kind}' on this page. If it is a list, register or menu, do not extract it "
                       "again: open the entry you need (one of its links) and extract that page.")
        else:
            summary = _summary(kind, data)
        self._cache[key] = summary
        return summary

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- brief
    async def read_brief(self) -> None:
        brief = self.run["brief"]

    async def run_role(self, role: str, mission: Mission) -> Explorer | None:
        """The mission on the website the brief assigns to it. If its checklist is still incomplete, the same mission
        briefly on each other website, in a fresh tab: other software splits the information differently (e.g. the
        specification attached to the tender, the bidder Q&A on the supplier portal). Approvals stay in the mailbox
        (the brief defines their authority by sender) and materials in the ERP, so those missions stay home."""
        home = self.site_for(role)
        explorer = await self.run_mission(home, mission)
        if role not in REDISPATCH or not mission.progress:
            return explorer
        for site in self.other_sites(home):
            if mission.progress()[1] or self.evidence_end - time.time() < 120:
                break
            elsewhere = Mission(**{**mission.__dict__, "name": f"{mission.name}@{site.site_id}", "max_steps": 12,
                                   "context": mission.context + f"\n\nNOT FOUND COMPLETELY ON THE WEBSITE '{home.site_id}'. "
                                   f"Still missing:\n{mission.progress()[0]}\nLook for exactly this on THIS website: it may "
                                   "be a document, an attachment, a message or a notice here. If this website does not "
                                   "have it, finish at once and list it as missing."})
            try:
                tab = await site.spawn()
            except Exception as error:   # never share a tab another mission is using
                log("redispatch_tab_failed", mission=mission.name, site=site.site_id, error=str(error)[:200])
                continue
            log("mission_redispatch", mission=mission.name, site=site.site_id)
            try:
                explorer = await self.explore_once(tab, elsewhere) or explorer
            finally:
                try:
                    await tab.page.close()
                except Exception:
                    pass
        if mission.progress()[1]:
            self.status[mission.name] = "complete"
        return explorer

    def other_sites(self, home: Site) -> list[Site]:
        """Every other website once, in the brief's role order (portals first), then any without a role."""
        seen, others = {home.site_id}, []
        for site in [self.site_for(r) for r in ("tender", "specification", "mail", "erp")] + list(self.sites.values()):
            if site.site_id not in seen:
                seen.add(site.site_id)

"""Structured logging: one JSON object per line on stdout (the platform shows stdout in the run log)."""
import json
import time

_T0 = time.monotonic()
MAX_LINE = 1500
KEEP_WHOLE = {"brief", "answer"}       # the facts a run is diagnosed from


def elapsed() -> float:
    return time.monotonic() - _T0


def log(event: str, **fields) -> None:
    line = {"t": round(elapsed(), 2), "event": event, **fields}
    # Short lines: the platform keeps only the most recent part of a long stdout, and the start of a run matters too.
    text = json.dumps(line, ensure_ascii=False, default=str)
    print(text if event in KEEP_WHOLE else text[:MAX_LINE], flush=True)

async def _do_click(self, ref: str) -> str:
        frame, el = await self._element(ref)
        tag = await el.evaluate("e => e.tagName")
        href = await el.get_attribute("href") if tag == "A" else None
        if href and not href.startswith(("#", "javascript:")):
            if await self.goto(urljoin(frame.url, href), frame=None if frame == self.page.main_frame else frame):
                return f"opened {href}"
            return f"ERROR: {href} did not load (the website did not answer in time); retry once or take another route"
        pages_before = set(self.context.pages)
        try:
            await el.click(timeout=5000)
        except PlaywrightError:
            await self._run_guards_everywhere("close_overlays")
            try:
                await el.click(timeout=4000)
            except PlaywrightError:
                await el.dispatch_event("click")
        await asyncio.sleep(0.3)
        folded = await self._fold_popups(pages_before)
        return "clicked" + (f"; {folded}" if folded else "")

    async def _fold_popups(self, pages_before: set) -> str:
        """A new window (window.open, target=_blank) is loaded in our tab instead, so the model keeps one view."""
    async def _do_type(self, ref: str, text: str, submit: bool = False) -> str:
        _, el = await self._element(ref)
        if problem := await self._ready(el):
            return problem
        await el.fill(str(text), timeout=4000)
        value = await el.input_value()
        if submit:
            await el.press("Enter")
            await asyncio.sleep(0.3)
        return f"typed; field now contains {value!r}" + (" and pressed Enter" if submit else "")

    async def _do_press_key(self, key: str, ref: str | None = None) -> str:
        pages_before = set(self.context.pages)
        if ref:
            _, el = await self._element(ref)
            await el.press(str(key), timeout=4000)
        else:
            await self.page.keyboard.press(str(key))
        await asyncio.sleep(0.4)
        folded = await self._fold_popups(pages_before)
        return f"pressed {key}" + (f"; {folded}" if folded else "")

async def _do_fill_form(self, fields: list, apply: str | None = None, then_click: str | None = None) -> str:
        """A whole form step in one call, addressed by the labels the model reads (refs change after every apply).
        Fields are set in the given order; a field that is still disabled is unlocked by pressing the form's apply
        button first, and after a choice the apply button is pressed when later fields are still disabled (cascading
        filters). Finally `then_click` (e.g. next) is pressed. Every value is read back."""
        results, applied = [], 0
        for index, field in enumerate(fields or []):
            label, value = str(field.get("field") or field.get("label") or ""), field.get("value")
            text = await self.observe(limit=200000)
            control, problem = _find_control(text, label, FIELD_KINDS)
            if control and control["disabled"] and apply and applied < 2 * len(fields):
                applied += 1
                await self._press(apply)
                text = await self.observe(limit=200000)
                control, problem = _find_control(text, label, FIELD_KINDS)
            if not control:
                results.append(f"{label}: ERROR {problem}")
                continue
            if control["disabled"] and not apply:
                buttons = " | ".join(f'"{c}"' for c in _control_names(text, BUTTON_KINDS)[:15])
                results.append(f"{label}: ERROR disabled until an earlier choice is applied: call again with "
                               f"apply=<the form's apply button>. Buttons on this page: {buttons}")
                continue
            ref = control["ref"]
            if control["kind"] == "select":
                outcome = await self._select(ref, str(value))
            elif control["kind"] in ("checkbox", "radio"):
                outcome = await self._do_check(ref, str(value).lower() not in ("false", "0", "no", "nein", ""))
            else:
                outcome = await self._do_type(ref, str(value))
            results.append(f"{label}: {outcome}")
            if apply and control["kind"] == "select" and not outcome.startswith("ERROR") and index + 1 < len(fields):
                later = [_find_control(text, str(f.get("field") or f.get("label") or ""), FIELD_KINDS)[0]
                         for f in fields[index + 1:]]
                if any(c and c["disabled"] for c in later) and applied < 2 * len(fields):
                    applied += 1
                    await self._press(apply)
        if then_click and any(": ERROR" in line for line in results):
            results.append(f"then {then_click}: NOT pressed because of the errors above. Fix only the failed fields "
                           "(with fill_form again), then press it.")
        elif then_click:
            results.append(f"then {then_click}: " + await self._press(then_click))
        return "\n".join(results)

    async def _press(self, label: str) -> str:
        """Click a button/link by its visible label and wait until the page has reacted (reload or DOM update)."""

content.text:
Here's what went wrong and what I changed. It's all uncommitted and nothing is submitted.

**Why you got 10/100 (`run_3c89f883ad003331`):** the specification mission failed. It kept "extracting revisions" from the supplier portal's *list of documents* (20 times) and never opened the specification itself. With no requirements there were no catalogue groups, so the ERP never ran and the bid went in with zero positions. That left 5 for the decision plus 5 for the reference. On top of that, the run stopped looking at 5:16 and submitted the empty bid at 6:11, with about 12 minutes of budget left. The same failure hit `run_f33ba429…` earlier: roughly 1 run in 4.

**Fixes for that:**
- **The spec mission finds the document first.** The goal, the checklist and the `read_all_pages` tool text now say lists have no revisions: browse them without extracting, then open the specification. After two "nothing found" extractions, the checklist says so explicitly.
  - In both local runs since the fix, it found and opened the specification within 5 steps and completed on the first attempt: 9 steps at 1:37, where it previously took 16 steps or failed.
- **It no longer gives up early.** Tender and specification missions get extra attempts while time remains. If the computed bid has no positions and at least 4 minutes are left, it doesn't submit yet; it runs one more recovery round.

**Further problems found while testing locally, also fixed:**
- **Slow pages:** a click or Enter that loads a slow page (8 s or more) counted as an error and could be repeated, so a form could be submitted twice. The tab was also sent back a page, which cost ~2 min in the mail mission. The agent now waits for the page properly, and a replaced tab reloads the page it was on.
- **Endless model replies:** both copies of a call hung for 150 s. Every call now has an output cap (3.5× the longest real answer seen in 554 calls). The backup request uses a different temperature, and each page in an `extract_urls` step has its own 75 s limit.
- **A slot-leak bug:** a cancelled model call never gave its concurrency slot back. After 10 such cancellations every model call would have blocked. Fixed.
- **`fill_form`** now applies a choice even when the model splits a position across two calls, accepts a ref in place of a label, and matches "keine" to "Ohne Zertifizierung".
- **Mail search:** the checklist now asks for one search on the reference first, which finds all topics at once, before any topic-by-topic searches. It shows the German subject keyword, not the English topic name.
- **Logs:** lines are now capped at 1,500 characters (the brief and answer are kept whole), so the platform stops dropping the start of each run.

**Checks:** 68 unit tests (11 new) and 176 dev tests pass, and the leak check is clean. The last local dry run scored **100/100**, with the review check verifying all 44 fields. Changes made after that run are covered by unit tests only.

One local-only issue I didn't fix: the tender portal session sometimes expires mid-submission locally, which forces a restart of the bid form. The resets come at random times across sites, which fits other teams using the same shared scouting login. The sandbox gives each run its own login, and your 11:39 scored run shows no re-login.

**Next, yours:** with nothing else running on the team (it shares the Qwen queue), run it 3 times:
```bash
atira test-run ./agent --challenge rfq --follow
```
Submit only if all 3 score 100. The local model proxy is still running in the background; tell me if you want it stopped.

content.text:
The code didn't change. **The websites were overloaded during this run.** The same package did 6:22 when the sites were calm.

From the run's own log:
- **The ERP returned `HTTP 503` ("service unavailable") six times** (5:21, 5:26, 6:28, 6:48 twice, 8:03). Each one costs a retry and a fresh tab.
- **The mail site timed out** (15 s page loads that never answered) at 2:00, 2:16, 8:08, 8:23 and 8:40.
- As a result, specification and tender finished only at **4:59 and 5:02**, against about 1:30 in a normal run. The ERP couldn't start before then, and at 8:40 it was still working, so the run was nowhere near submitting when you cancelled it.

Why the sites were slow: at least **5 team test runs were running at the same time** (19:24–19:55), and every one of them failed. Each run drives 4 browsers against the same four servers, and other teams are hitting them too, which is likely the end-of-hackathon rush. The model queue wasn't the problem this time (median call 3.2 s).

So nothing in the code needs fixing for this. To get a clean measurement:
- Make sure **nobody on the team has a run going**: check `atira status`, or the team page.
- Run **one** test and **don't cancel it early**. Under load it may take 10+ minutes but can still finish and score.

If you're about to submit for the final, do it when nothing else of the team is running. The scored run is a single attempt, and the latest submission that passes review is the one that counts.
